clue.text: Former partner takes exercise alongside unusual diet to make things happen

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the word beside it is taken out of its ordinary order

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's ex starts working out on a strange diet in order to get results.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to speed matters along, causing action to occur promptly rather than stalling.

clue.text: Key flight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Esc button on a computer keyboard
second meaning: a getaway or breakout

explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard button is named after the word, which also means running away from danger or captivity.

clue.text: Goes round to block up drip internally

indicators.note: internally means placed inside, so the drip goes within the other word
in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to block is to stop
an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: Someone moves around to plug a leaking drip from inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' suggests a leak; in crosswords it is usually the hospital drip that feeds fluid into a vein.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivots means turns on a central point, rotating like a hinge or swivel.

clue.text: Starts to describe indigenous native growling Ozzie

definitions.text: Starts to describe indigenous native growling Ozzie

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, so the initial of each following word is taken

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: The opening words of a description of a snarling wild Australian animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a snarling native Australian wild dog. Ozzie is a spelling of Aussie, Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog, a native creature that growls, so the full sentence describes it.

clue.text: Fit French aunt didn't finish drink

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: tante is French for aunt
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A healthy French relative left her drink unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective for the aunt; it is the noun, an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a sudden childish outburst of rage, a fit of temper.

clue.text: Raved about bachelor unduly perhaps

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: Someone ranted about an unmarried man, perhaps excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unduly' reads as a comment on the raving, but it is an example of the answer's word class, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unduly is a word ending in -ly that modifies verbs, so it serves as one instance of this grammatical category.

clue.text: Terribly bad credit? Use this instead

definitions.text: Terribly bad credit? Use this instead

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to someone with a poor credit record: pay another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: with a bad credit history, you pay with this plastic instead of a credit card.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit card takes money straight from a bank account, so it is the alternative when borrowing is not possible.

clue.text: About to reveal what helps Americans get to the top

definitions.text: what helps Americans get to the top

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip on how Americans climb to success, about to be disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to the top' suggests ambition; literally it is riding up a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word for what Britons call a lift, carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Somehow obtain good person who is an expert on bloomers

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the next word's letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ST, saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Somehow acquire a decent sort who knows all about knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are old-fashioned women's knickers; here they are things that bloom, flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants, including flowering ones that bloom.

clue.text: Agreement between spelling group and social worker

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches, who cast spells
ants are social insects and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: A pact drawn up between a witches' circle and a council care worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a job in social services; in crosswords it is often the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding promise or contract between parties, a solemn pact.

clue.text: A series of books about bovine disease is missing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the series of books wraps around the disease

parts.note: taken as written
the New Testament is a collection of biblical books
bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A volume set on cattle illness has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Testament is the usual crossword source for a series of books; the single A stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent describes someone or something not present, gone or lacking from where expected.

clue.text: Speak impolitely about Norfolk town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for disrespect or insult
second meaning: a market town in Norfolk, an English county

explanation.surface: Someone is rude about a town in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb means insult or disrespect someone, and it is also the name of a small market town in East Anglia.

clue.text: Award for French state is an aromatic assortment

parts.note: a pot is a trophy cup
pour is French for 'for'
RI is the postal code for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A prize given for a French region turns out to be a fragrant medley.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for scent, and by extension any mixed collection.

clue.text: Coach self-discipline to give up siesta outside

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so those letters are removed from the longer word
outside says the letters dropped sit at both ends, wrapped around what is kept

parts.note: restraint is control over oneself
a siesta is an afternoon rest

explanation.surface: A trainer tells someone to show self-control and stop taking naps.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed word is split, part at the front and one letter at the back, which is why 'outside' is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to instruct and drill them, teaching skills through practice.

clue.text: Space for bear's friend to get married

parts.note: Roo is the young kangaroo, a friend of Winnie-the-Pooh
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A venue is needed so a bear's pal can hold his wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is Winnie-the-Pooh, whose companions include Kanga and Roo.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available capacity or area, as in 'there is no room'.

clue.text: Connoisseur's glasses contain small measure with Greek character and lime zest

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so the measure goes inside the glasses

parts.note: a pair of spectacle lenses, drawn as two O shapes
an en is a printer's unit of width
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: zest is the outer peel of a citrus fruit, so the word's outer letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: An expert's drinking glasses hold a tot mixed with a Greek spirit and lime peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' tempts toward wine glasses, apt for the answer; here it means spectacles, drawn as two round lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and expert of wine, a connoisseur of vintages.

clue.text: Traces dogs' companions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: faint signs or hints of something
second meaning: those who dog someone, following them everywhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' looks like the animals, but it is the verb meaning follows closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadows can be slight vestiges, and also people who tail a person constantly like a detective or close follower.

clue.text: Predicts time when reporters go round

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the press, reporters collectively
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A forecaster foresees the moment journalists will circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or be a warning sign of something to come.

clue.text: Broadly embracing weather protection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covering many things, as in an overall term or organisation
second meaning: a folding canopy held over one's head in rain

explanation.surface: A warm wide hug that keeps out the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means all-encompassing, as in an over-arching body; as a noun it is the familiar rain shield.

clue.text: Love Italian cafe surroundings

parts.note: a Roman is someone from Rome, in Italy

indicators.note: the surroundings of a word are its outermost letters, the ones on the edges

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A romantic setting: falling for someone in an Italian coffee shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance means a loving relationship or the passionate feeling between lovers.

clue.text: Existence, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: a word that is the same from either direction reads identically in both

parts.note: Latin for 'to be', used in English for being

explanation.surface: A philosophical shrug: life is the same from any angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alone yields the word; the rest of the clue confirms it reads identically from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is the philosophical term for being, essential nature or actual existence.

clue.text: Every year police officer gets protection

parts.note: per annum, Latin for each year
a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: Each year a constable is given armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun read as a plural: pads together give protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads are cushioned guards worn by players, as in cricket, to shield the body from blows.

clue.text: Cut up fat and remove crown

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim fat and take the top off something.
explanation.walkthrough: LOP reversed gives POL, then LARD. 'Crown' suggests a king; it is the top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To pollard a tree is to cut its upper branches back to the trunk, lopping its head.

clue.text: Fresher environment reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

parts.note: an area is a surrounding zone

explanation.surface: A cleaner, fresher setting, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound nearly the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Airier means better ventilated, with more breeze, so the air feels fresher.

clue.text: Worms discovered in cabin chest

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so the letters are within the following words

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Worms turned up in a box in a ship's cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worms' looks like a plural noun; it is the verb, crawls slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To worm one's way is to move slowly and carefully forward, creeping along bit by bit.

clue.text: Band brought back "Bits & Pieces"

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: bits and pieces are parts, components

explanation.surface: A music group reformed under the name Bits & Pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits & Pieces' looks like a band name in quotation marks; it is the wordplay, and Band is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric used to fasten or hold, a band in the physical sense.

clue.text: Alison confused about tax redemption

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged name surrounds the tax
confused letters are jumbled, so the name is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A woman named Alison is baffled by a tax rebate.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged name splits into two parts with the tax sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is deliverance from sin or harm, the religious sense of being saved or rescued.

clue.text: Sound system adds nothing to car

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A car stereo that contributes nothing to the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio refers to equipment for reproducing recorded music and voices, like a hi-fi.

clue.text: French singer returned after third of August

indicators.note: third of picks out the single letter in position three of the following word

parts.note: the third letter

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the singer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cilla Black, the Liverpool pop singer and TV host

explanation.surface: A French vocalist came home after the start of August.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool pop singer, later a British TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic is an adjective for things of France, from Gaul, the old Roman name for the region.

clue.text: Opponents in charge of hospital food

parts.note: South and West sit as opponents at the bridge table
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
H is the map sign for a hospital

explanation.surface: Rival managers running a hospital's catering.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so S and W are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is a snack of fillings between bread slices, an everyday item to eat.

clue.text: Bowler changes end to get ratings

indicators.note: changing the end means swapping the final letter for a different one

parts.note: a seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball move off its seam

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler switches ends to improve his scores.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R becomes N. 'Changes end' in cricket means bowling from the other end; here it alters the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratings are ordinary naval sailors without officer rank, a nautical sense crosswords use often.

clue.text: Defers notice — press have nothing to lose

parts.note: an ad, a notice in a paper

indicators.note: having to lose nothing means a zero-shaped letter is dropped

parts.note: journos is slang for journalists, the press
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A newspaper postpones an announcement because the reporters have nothing at stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn is to postpone proceedings until later, suspending a meeting to another time.
